text:
nina.sales: Heads-up — POC for ClearBank is stuck. Their integration team reports that our JS and Python SDKs hang when users are behind corporate proxies. They see the first chunk then nothing. Need a quick triage so we can get them to sign the SOW.
oscar.eng: Which SDK versions and transports did they try? stream vs poll? Any client logs or server request-ids?
nina.sales: Python 1.0.0rc, node-sdk 0.8.3, both with stream enabled. They tried both HTTP streaming and ws on different clients. Node errors show socket resets; Python shows iterator blocking. Minimal logs attached by them (pasted below).
mei-sre: Paste the logs here and their proxy type if known — Zscaler/BlueCoat/F5 etc. Also ask if they require Kerberos/NTLM or any custom CA.
nina.sales: They said "corporate-proxy.company.com" (F5 in front, Zscaler cloud behind). Proxy does TLS inspection and enforces SSO (Kerberos). Logs:
```
# node-client
POST /v1/chat 200
chunk 1 received
error: socket hang up (ECONNRESET)

# python-client
INFO:response: got chunk
# then hangs forever, no exception, app waiting on async for loop
```
oscar.eng: Two likely culprits: 1) proxy is buffering/chopping chunked transfer-encoding frames, 2) proxy is terminating and re-issuing TLS which breaks streamed TLS tunnels. Quick repro steps:
- Ask them to curl our endpoint through proxy with --http1.1 and --no-buffering: `curl -v --http1.1 --no-buffer --proxy http://corporate-proxy:8080 https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
- Try `curl --raw` to show raw chunk frames.
- Check if proxy rewrites Transfer-Encoding or strips Connection: keep-alive.

tarun-dev: If proxy requires Kerberos, many HTTP client libraries add extra auth bytes that confuse chunk parsing. For Node, try `agent: new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true })` and set `headers: { 'Connection': 'keep-alive' }`. For Python, ensure `stream=True` and set smaller read timeouts so we surfice errors back to the app.

nina.sales: They ran curl and got 502 after ~18s. Output:
```
* Connected to corporate-proxy 10.2.2.2:8080
> CONNECT inference.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
mei-sre: 502 on CONNECT + TLS inspection + Kerberos = classic stream breakage. Ask if they can temporarily add a bypass (no TLS inspection) for inference.redwood.ai. If policy forbids this, request a proxy rule that allows raw CONNECT tunnels to that FQDN/port.

oscar.eng: Short-term workaround: flip POC to non-streaming (polling) mode so they can validate correctness and cost. Longer term we should add a client-side fallback: detect stalled stream (no bytes in X seconds) -> cancel stream and switch to polling endpoint automatically (with telemetry emitted).

tarun-dev: We can add a quick flag in both SDKs `redwoodClient({ streamFallback: true, streamTimeout: 20 })` to enable the behavior. I'll prototype today.

security-bot: Reminder: before recommending bypasses, we need A) customer signoff in ticket, B) an RFC that documents risks. I'll attach SOC2 excerpts and cert-pinning docs they can show to their infra team.

nina.sales: From deal ops side — they need streaming latency numbers to decide on Dedicated vs Hosted. If infra will add a proxy exception we can proceed. Else, we need to show a roadmap and interim mitigation (SDK fallback + security attestation) to keep the deal moving.
oscar.eng: Action items: 1) nina to collect curl --raw output + proxy config + sample request-id, 2) tarun to push SDK fallback flag prototype + instructions for node/python, 3) mei to draft a one-page proxy checklist for their infra (exact host, ports, headers to allow), 4) security-bot to attach SOC2/KMS notes. I'll also try to reproduce with a local mitm proxy configured for Kerberos.

nina.sales: I'll send the checklist to ClearBank infra and ask for a short window to test bypass. Also looping legal for a temporary exception signoff. Thanks team. :pray:
